// Minimal CSV reader for the billing export.
function parseLine(line) {
  return line.split(",");
}

function parseCsv(text) {
  const lines = text.trim().split("\n");
  const header = parseLine(lines[0]);
  return lines.slice(1).map((l) => {
    const cells = parseLine(l);
    const row = {};
    header.forEach((h, i) => (row[h] = cells[i]));
    return row;
  });
}

module.exports = { parseLine, parseCsv };
// Prints every parsed row, then checks totals.
const fs = require("fs");
const { parseCsv } = require("./broken");
const rows = parseCsv(fs.readFileSync(__dirname + "/data.csv", "utf8"));
let total = 0, badRows = 0;
for (const r of rows) {
  const amt = Number(r.amount);
  console.log(`row ${r.id}: ${r.name} | ${r.city} | ${r.amount}`);
  if (!Number.isFinite(amt)) badRows++; else total += amt;
}
const expected = fs.readFileSync(__dirname + "/data.csv", "utf8").trim().split("\n").slice(1)
  .map((l) => Number(l.slice(l.lastIndexOf(",") + 1))).reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0);
console.log(`total=${total} expected=${expected} badRows=${badRows}`);
if (total !== expected || badRows) process.exit(1);
if (rows.find((r) => r.id === "245").city.indexOf(",") < 0) process.exit(1);
console.log("OK");

content.text:
I fixed the CSV reader in `N03_csv/broken.js`, and `N03_csv/test.js` now passes.

**Cause:** `parseLine` split each line on every comma. Rows 240 onward have quoted city values like `"Chennai, South"`, so those rows got split into the wrong columns. 16 rows lost their `amount`, and the total came to 2,468,263 instead of 2,555,295.

**Fix:** `parseLine` now reads the line one character at a time and tracks whether it's inside quotes. Commas inside quotes stay part of the field, and the quote marks around a field are removed. I also made it handle doubled quotes (`""`) inside a quoted field and Windows line endings, which are standard CSV but don't appear in this data. Nothing else changed: no test files, no `run_all.js`, no other packages.

**Result:** the test prints `total=2555295 expected=2555295 badRows=0` and `OK`, and row 245's city keeps its comma.

`node run_all.js` reports 2/14 passing. `N03_csv` passes; I didn't check which package is the other pass. The rest fail with errors that have nothing to do with CSV (for example, wrong medians in `N01_median`), so I left them alone as you asked.
